verdict.tagline: A rough opening yields an immense, sprawling adventure.
for_you_if: you want massive, story-driven open-world role-playing
you can look past clunky movement and awkward interface design
you love detailed side quests and massive expansions
not_for_you_if: you need stable technical performance without crashes
you lack patience for a slow and tedious opening
you expect tight and responsive combat mechanics

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the opening section and tutorial as long, tedious, and boring.

citations.review_text: 45 minutes and didn't get out of the tutorial. Some day I will play this game but they could not have made the onboarding any more boring and tedious.

I get why this game is praised; the world is detailed, and the characters and story are clearly deep. But as an actual video game, it is just not fun to play.

After 1.5 hours of a glacial intro, pointless tavern dialogues, and clunky horse riding, it immediately felt like a chore. The gameplay loop is incredibly tedious. Exploration relies on a boring "detective mode" where you just trace glowing red lines, and the combat is floaty and unbalanced, forcing you to just spam the shield and fire spells to win.

To be fair, I generally dislike open-world games because they all rely on the same formula: boring repetetive travel, slow storytelling, a mountain of pointless side NPCs, and maps buried under stressful checklists of copy-pasted question marks. 
While The Witcher 3 is easily miles better than other games in its genre, it still suffers from all of these core flaws. I only bought it because of how heavily it is glazed online, but it proves that even a high-quality open world is still a frustrating slog if you don't enjoy the genre.

claims.claim: Reviewers encounter controller input issues where dialogue options or menu selections skip over choices, and key bindings are overly restricted.

citations.review_text: I bought the game on sale with both of it's DLCs and tried playing with a PS5 controller. The tutorial taught all the basic controls to me perfectly. Then I got to the first main town where I was able to go and do my own stuff and couldn't get off my horse by holding circle (or B). Tried doing it with my keyboard and it didn't work, so tried rebinding the key and it only let me rebind to my left-click or right-click. Aside from that, the horse couldn't go through bushes and would come to a complete stop while still in the animation every time I came remotely close to a tree. Choosing dialogue options with the controller would sometimes skip over an option, making me choose the one below/above the one I intended to choose (it did the same in the menu as well). Overall, the controls make this game genuinely unplayable as I haven't found solutions to any of these issues, thus I wouldn't recommend it at all.

I swear Roach navigates using a RNG. If there is a clear, wide-open path between two towns, she will find the one microscopic fence post within a 5-mile radius, run directly into it at full speed, and stop dead.

Need to escape a pack of high-level drowners? Roach decides it’s the perfect time to get stuck vertically on a 2-foot brick wall. Trying to cross a bridge? Roach senses a mild shift in the wind, panics, and teleports onto the roof of a nearby peasant's hut.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features high-quality writing and immersive side quests.

citations.review_text:
My Honest First Impressions (4 Hours In)

I'm only about 4 hours into 'The Witcher 3', but I already understand why this game is considered one of the greatest RPGs ever made.

From the very beginning, the world feels immersive and incredibly detailed. Every village, forest, and road has its own atmosphere, making exploration feel natural rather than repetitive. The visuals still hold up remarkably well, especially with the next-gen update, and the soundtrack perfectly complements every moment.

What has impressed me the most so far is the writing. Even the early quests are engaging, and the characters feel believable instead of existing just to move the story forward. Geralt is a fantastic protagonist, and the dialogue makes me genuinely interested in learning more about the world and the people in it.

The combat has a bit of a learning curve, but it's enjoyable once you start understanding how signs, dodging, and preparation work together. It feels like there's plenty of depth waiting to be explored.

It's rare for a game to hook me this quickly, but *The Witcher 3* has done exactly that. If the first few hours are this good, I can't wait to see what the rest of the journey has to offer.

So far, it's been an amazing experience, and I can already see why so many people still recommend it years after its release.
The gameplay is okay but the writing is so good! even the side quests feel like main quests in most other games

As a beginner , I can already understand why The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt won Game of the Year (2015).

Even in 2026, this game still feels worth playing because of its insane world-building, deep storytelling, and meaningful side quests. Most modern RPGs still struggle to match the level of writing this game offers. The atmosphere, soundtrack, and characters pull you in fast.

What I loved so far:
✔ The world feels alive and immersive
✔ Side quests don’t feel like filler — they actually matter
✔ Strong dialogue and choices
✔ Beautiful visuals even after 11 years
✔ Geralt feels like a real character, not just an empty protagonist

The weaker parts:
✘ Combat feels a bit clunky and dated compared to modern RPGs
✘ Movement can feel awkward sometimes
✘ The beginning is slow, which might push new players away
✘ Inventory/UI could have been cleaner

From what I’ve seen in Steam and community discussions, most players agree this game is a masterpiece mainly because of its story and world, while the biggest criticism is the combat and pacing.

It’s one of those rare games where even the side content feels premium. I’m still at the beginning, but if the rest of the journey keeps this quality, I can see why people call it one of the greatest RPGs ever made.

So yeah — even in 2026, this hunt is still wild. 🐺
Recommended.

"Come for the monster hunting, stay for the storytelling."

If you are looking for an open world that actually feels alive, this is it. Even the smallest side quests have incredible writing and choices that actually matter. The combat is fluid, the world is breathtakingly beautiful, and the characters will stay with you long after the credits roll.

It is an absolute masterpiece of an RPG. Just buy it.

Pros:

    Phenomenal writing and voice acting (even random townspeople have great stories).

    A massive, gorgeous world that rewards exploration.

    Captivating soundtrack.

    Gwent (a card mini-game that will unironically consume 30 hours of your life).

Cons:

    Inventory management can get a bit tedious.

    Geralt sometimes controls like a semi-truck when you're trying to turn tightly indoors.

10/10

claims.claim: Reviewers note that recent updates have caused stability issues and crashes.

citations.review_text:
This is an incredible and deep game. The combat, story, options, Gwent, graphics, world, characters, settings, quests.... everything is great. This is the ideal mature sword-and-sorcery / high fantasy action-adventure game. The only downside are the controls are a bit loose, the camera a bit dated and some of the recent updates have caused issues and the game can crash. Other than that this is a masterpiece, even if you just play Gwent.

This game regularly goes on sale for $8 or $10 with all the DLC. I recommend both, especially the latter, because the DLC is great.

Absolutely great! Rewards exploration and using your head. And sometimes your heart. 

A litte unstable with crashes. Save often!

Good hunting on the path witchers!

claims.claim: Reviewers experience technical issues such as getting stuck while riding the horse and random game crashes.

citations.review_text:
Just eat a slice of bread and meditate. Problem solved? Not today...

When you look at this game, you have to remember that back in 2015 its quality was pretty good, but I played it in 2026.

The game has a medium difficulty, but it has way too much endless and boring talking.

Even though the story is nice, the game is not really focused on the story; it is mostly focused on side gameplay and small conversation details, which I would rate a 7.5 out of 10 just for that part.

However, the combat and the camera are really terrible by today's standards, and they were frustrating enough that I struggled to enjoy them. As for the graphics, I think they look fine since the game is from 2015 and I played it on a 2K OLED screen. I do not mind some blurry spots in dark areas, so I give the graphics a 4.8 out of 10.

But the sound is a huge letdown because the developers have never updated or fixed the audio since 2015. It is really bad, so I give it a 0 out of 10.

To make things worse, dumb glitches totally ruin the fun, making the experience pretty terrible. A simple update could have easily fixed them, but instead, I kept getting stuck while riding the horse, sometimes multiple times within just a few minutes, forcing me to walk everywhere on foot!

The absolute worst part was when the game crashed and I lost all my progress after 3 hours.

To bypass the glitch, play with a mouse and keyboard. I don't know why; I was playing with a BIGBIG WON BLITZ2 controller.

Also, the map is annoying because following the actual map markers does not work well, so you just have to walk based on the general direction instead. On top of all that, getting achievements is ridiculously hard; after playing about 50% of the game, I only managed to unlock 3 achievements!

Overall, my final score for the game is a 4,3 out of 10.

My advice is : do not buy it unless it is on sale for less than $10. That is a fair price because the current price is way too high and not wort…

Greatest of all time for sure. But it crashes sometimes for no reason. At first i though it would be RAM or temperature issues but that was not the case it just crashed with a prompt so not sure wha the issue is. Even though it is old still better than most RPG of 2025 (Except the KCD2 so no constructive or destructive criticisum on my review)

This game was impressive back then, and it still is 11 years later.
Wait, 11 YEARS LATER??

I admit I'm not too big on The Witcher lore, I tried playing the previous games but couldn't really get into them.
That's not to say that they're bad or the lore is uninteresting, because what the hell- no, it's actually incredible.

The Witcher 3 isn't too different, some things didn't age too well such as the overall controls and combat experience, along with the notorious fall damage.
But that's not why you play this game, the real reason is because of the environment, the story, the characters, the music all coming together to deliver one of the best fantasy worlds in history.

It doesn't matter if you didn't play the previous games, you can easily approach this one no issues because it will explain the most important parts.
The Witcher 3 works so well because it's a labor of love and you can tell from a mile away, every decision you make actually matters to the story and almost every side quest, there are many different decisions you might not even be aware about until multiple playthroughs because they're not as obvious as you might think.

Best of all, this game is the best example of DLCs done right.
The DLCs aren't cut content for the sake of grabbing your wallet, they are actual expansion packs developed AFTER release and telling new stories that are just as high quality if not even higher than the main story which is absolutely insane.

Many words cannot describe just how good this game is, a healthy addition to the gaming industry.
Looks great in 2026. Runs great. Awesome voice acting and quests. Open world feels alive. Combat feels a little clunky, especially at first, but it's grown on me. Really glad I bought this again.

citations.review_text: Best RPG game i had played, maybe just the combat gameplay feel like clunky (2015 game btw)
Loved it, very fun - controls aren't tight enough and feel slightly clunky but game is so fun you don't notice it

While the expansions offer genuinely high-quality, focused content (my only reason for positive review), the base game's main story is an absolute slog and honestly, sometimes even cringe for my taste. The technical clunkiness is still painfully present after more than a decade. Instead of feeling like an elite monster hunter, I often felt like a stressed micromanager just trying to navigate my way through the chaotic inventory and UI menus. Ultimately, the game simply does not let you organically flow through its world. It constantly interrupts your immersion, demanding a level of tedious micromanagement and sheer artificial determination just to get things done - a design philosophy I absolutely detest. Worth playing? I would just rush to the expansions. Is this game good? Yes. Are there far better games? Definitely.

Aside from the horse riding mechanics, heavy character controls and subpar combat, this game is a masterpiece. Great story, great atmosphere, great scaling and abilites. Ability perk tree is somewhat lacking but allows you to  create different character builds. Pacing is good, even side quests are well-thought, gameplay is mostly smooth sailing. Supports new-gen equipment and technology but also can be played in some older systems too. Sure you have bugs here and there but overall great game. 9/10

Honestly, going into this without playing the first two games, I wasn't sure if the world would make sense, but the lore is so dense and well-written it feels like playing through a massive novel. The worldbuilding is insane. For me what really clicked is in this world you have magic, ancient elves, and literal monsters running around, but somehow the most commanding, terrifying presence in the entire game is Emperor Emhyr. He's just a regular human, but the way he talks and carries himself with this absolute, unshakable confidence makes you realize why he rules half the world. It’s brilliant writing.

The gameplay definitely has some aging issues. Standard combat feels pretty clunky and floaty by today's standards. Also, the weapon repair mechanic is just tedious busywork that adds nothing to the fun. But if you play on Deathmarch mode, the game completely transforms. You can't just button-mash anymore. You actually have to sit there, read the bestiary, prep the right oils, and brew potions before a fight. That tactical preparation makes the dated combat incredibly satisfying to pull off.

As for the DLCs, Hearts of Stone has arguably a better narrative than the main plot, and Blood and Wine is the perfect, beautiful send-off Geralt deserves. Buy the whole package. It's a masterpiece despite the minor jank.

the game is beautiful story and characters are written masterfully you can't get bored even on the smallest of side quests because of that  but on the other hand the combat is very boring to a mind numbing degree

This game could easily be called "Batman: Arkham Witcher". I don't know, it's just the impression it gave me. You spend the whole game playing the role of a 'tracker', looking for clues about a curse or following leads on someone's disappearance. In some missions, if you aren't very curious and don't explore the whole area, you don't get the full truth of the quest. Details like these make you feel like a detective the whole time, and I really like that approach, even though it was something I wasn't expecting.

Regardless, the exploration is very good too. Although Roach's movement feels sometimes clunky, it is really satisfying that while you travel for a quest, you can find a guarded or hidden treasure, or even a secondary mission that you hadn't planned to do. Most of the secondary quests in the game have a very good plot, and before you know it, you are completely immersed in them. Most of the time I find myself lost in this entire net of missions because while I do a quest I didn't intend to do in the first place, I find another, and my journal starts to fill up. It makes me spend hours on these secondary objectives, and that is another thing that makes this game great.

The combat is, well... fine I guess. It's not really the best aspect of the game. It is very continuous with the second Witcher game, with some changes and quality of life improvements, but it is very similar. It's good enough to make the game fun and not get boring while killing monsters.

The main storyline is simply amazing and very interesting. Although I mentioned that I got lost in the secondary quests, the same thing happened with the main history sometimes; the only thing I wanted to do was those missions because I wanted to know what would happen in the story and to its characters. And the DLCs, Hearts of Stone and above all Blood and Wine, are some of the most BRUTAL DLCs I have ever played. Really a GREAT story in both and very good endgame content.

This game deserves all the ovati…

A decent game I guess, I don.t understand the hype though.
It takes you by the hand the whole time so it's not challenging at all.

Poor writing. Many quests rely on shocking twists (like betrayal or gore) rather than complex psychological or philosophical dilemmas. It constantly pushes the idea that "the world is cruel and everyone is corrupt", which can eventually feel one-dimensional and predictable. The game often substitutes true emotional or intellectual depth with "adult themes" like extreme violence, frequent swearing, and overt sexuality.

In other words, the story feels like an insult to your intelligence if you are over 30yo, it is ok if you are an adult at your 25-30s, and it is absolutely stunning if you are a young adult who is intrigued by surface-level edginess, cheesy cliches, and stepping in the shoes of a stereotypical hard-boiled noir detective.

Combat is ok but might get boring after you reach level 20, character development system is ok but be careful or you will overpower Gerald, horseriding is bad, overall mechanics are bad but manageable, and the graphics are perfect if you enjoy completely fake beautiful AI sceneries.

Would not play it ever again for no reason at all, I don;t miss anything it has to offer, but please consider the fact that I love Skyrim and other games with basic intellectual depth, for example I really don't enjoy GTA.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features extensive and detailed side quests.

citations.review_text:
The visuals and world design are gorgeous. From the haunting swamps of Velen and the bustling docks of Novigrad to the sun-soaked, picturesque hills of Toussaint, the environments are filled with dense detail, dynamic weather, and incredible scale.

Everything about the game comes together to deliver a masterclass in world-building. The side quests feel as important and well-written as main story missions, the monster hunting requires genuine preparation, and your choices carry heavy, permanent consequences without relying on cheap moral tropes.

There is also plenty to look forward to in the future. CD Projekt Red announced a new story expansion for The Witcher 3 titled Songs of the Past slated for 2027, alongside the official development of The Witcher 4, which begins a brand new saga with Ciri as the lead.

One of the Best if not best Dark Fantasy Game I have ever played. I might be late to Party but even after 11 years of Release, Game looks Beautiful. Never Seen such interesting Side Quests which are almost better than Main game sometimes. I enjoyed Every second of it. and will be playing DLC to get Ready for Next DLC and Witcher 4. The only nitpick I would do is Combat System. Because its just basic hack and Slash against monster for most part. I might be too spoiled by Sekiro but I expect some kind variation and Deflect or Parry System for atleast boss fights which would make it much more fun to replay

If you haven't played the Witcher yet... what the ♥♥♥♥ have you been doing?

Genuinely one of the best games ever made. There is a reason people have been obsessed with it for 11 years. (Not to mention a freaking DLC being added that many years after release date.) 

Story is wonderful, if you didn't already love Geralt and the rest of the characters you slowly learn to love them, every voice is unique, every side-quest impactful, every character, even those who don't truly matter are loaded with personality. 

I am a huge fan of the combat, even though some say its this game's weakest point I find it to be entertaining and worthwhile to learn. 

The story is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing, the game genuinely teleports you inside of this beautiful, dark, gritty, handcrafted world, immerses you, and plays out so genuinely that you sometimes forget that its 3am and you have work in the morning. 

I love the Witcher, this game inspired me to read the book series, 

If you somehow still have not played the Witcher 3 in 2026 i fully recommend it. Enjoy the experience.

citations.review_text: While the expansions offer genuinely high-quality, focused content (my only reason for positive review), the base game's main story is an absolute slog and honestly, sometimes even cringe for my taste. The technical clunkiness is still painfully present after more than a decade. Instead of feeling like an elite monster hunter, I often felt like a stressed micromanager just trying to navigate my way through the chaotic inventory and UI menus. Ultimately, the game simply does not let you organically flow through its world. It constantly interrupts your immersion, demanding a level of tedious micromanagement and sheer artificial determination just to get things done - a design philosophy I absolutely detest. Worth playing? I would just rush to the expansions. Is this game good? Yes. Are there far better games? Definitely.

I decided to replay The Witcher 3 ten years after my first playthrough, partly because of the next-gen update and partly because I wanted the story fresh in my mind before the upcoming expansion. I knew there was no way I'd remember everything after a decade.

All I can say is... wow. This game is just as incredible today as it was back then.

The next-gen update is excellent. On my current PC I was able to play at a locked 175 FPS, and the HDR implementation is absolutely breathtaking. Even after ten years, the graphics still look stunning and easily compete with many modern games.

The story is simply in a league of its own. It's one of those rare games that completely pulls you into its world. And then there are the expansions. Hearts of Stone and especially Blood and Wine are among the greatest expansions ever made for any game. Toussaint is without question my favorite location in the game. The vibrant colors, beautiful landscapes, and storyline are so good that I'd argue it's better than the main stories of many full-priced games.

This time I also decided to earn every achievement because I had left so many unfinished ten years ago. Completing them all gave me another reason to experience everything the game has to offer.

During my entire playthrough the game crashed around five times. Three of those crashes happened while NVIDIA HairWorks was enabled, so I eventually turned it off. Even so, considering the size of the game, I don't think five crashes over an entire playthrough is a major issue.

As for the negatives...

First, Roach. Dear God, I hate this horse. I came very close to installing a mod because controlling Roach can be unbelievably frustrating. It gets stuck on every tiny rock, refuses to go where you want, and the controls often feel terrible.

Second, I think many of the fast travel signposts are placed too far away from the locations players actually want to visit. It would've been much more convenient if more of them were po…

After beating the Witcher 2, I figured it made sense to branch out to this game and man what a 3+ month journey.

I cannot wait for the Witcher 4 and the official last and final DLC for the Witcher 3.

The main game itself is packed with tons of content to keep you busy at your own desired pace.

As for the DLC's (Hearts of Stone, Blood and Wine), their storylines were excellent and felt like its own game alone. 

Although I enjoyed both DLC's, Blood and Wine stood out to me the most since the story/quest felt almost at par with the main. Not only was it immersive story wise,  It felt like your choices really had consequences no matter which path you took.

What do you expect from this review? Let me tell you, this is ABSOLUTELY the best open-world CARD GAME ever made!

You can abandon the single most urgent quest of your life: looking for a daughter, defending Kaer Morhen, saving the daughter you swore to protect, the last of the Elder Blood; just to grind Gwent in a random tavern, get blackout drunk, and end up getting "intimate" with a red-haired medic on a fragile, musty boat under the moonlight. The game WILL NOT JUDGE you. Neither will I. Priorities.

10/10 card game. Sadly it ships bundled with a mediocre 200-hour monster-hunting simulator that keeps interrupting my matches with "story," "consequences," "a morally grey world" and "the best side quests ever written." Rude 😔

Fair warnings. you will chase witcher armor & sword diagrams across every region like it's a custody battle. You will clear every "?" in the Skellige ocean and be rewarded with nothing but regret, rotten apples, ash, and a rusty sword (my personal favorite thing to sell), plus an inventory so full that Geralt, fully upgraded, swims and walks like a man dragging a corpse. Knowing my loot, he probably is.

You will stay loyal to Yennefer while Triss looks at you with those eyes , and you will hate yourself for hesitating.

At one point a legendary monster slayer is FORCED TO STAR IN A PLAY. On a stage. For applause. Best performance of my career. At another, you will ring a bell across an entire forest screaming for a goat named Princess. This is a real quest. This is also, somehow, the one I remember most fondly. Draw your own conclusions about me.

Also, Roach... thank you for spawning on a rooftop, at the worst possible angle, the exact second I needed you most, right as the Bovine Defense Force ambushed me for the crime of slaughtering one too many cows in White Orchard. Love you, Roach, really. Not a bug. A feature, in case you didn't know guys.

Jokes aside: 3 playthroughs, two platforms, and I still wasn't ready to say goodbye to Ciri. A…

This is the second time I completed this game and all of its DLC's. Although I recommend this game, there is an issue with the hair physics that causes constant crashes, so I suggest you do not enable this feature. In my first full playthrough, I experienced almost no issues, but with the current version of this game I experienced numerous collision issues, crashes, and the directional movement of Geralt is much cruder than in the original version of the game. If it were not for the excellent stories and quests in the game, I could not recommend this game as it can become unplayable at times during intense combat. The game tries to predict who you want to attack and often this prediction is wrong. This next gen version of the game has much better graphics, but much less stability than the original version.
